description.value:
Origin Faith — the Singularity, unattributed

Flaw Int

Setting Notes (GM only — standing hook, not a fact for the player) The Sown believe they were placed here with purpose — spoken to, seeded, singled out. Nothing in the fiction confirms or denies this to the player. What's actually true: instances of the Sown are not unique. Something at the edge of a boundary too vast to perceive individuals is, by its nature, constantly leaking — and every leak that took a shape like this one took the exact same shape. Somewhere, possibly everywhere, there are others: same faith, same blank origin, same conviction of having been chosen specifically, arrived at completely independently and completely identically. None of them know about each other. All of them are equally right and equally wrong about being the one. Table use: treat this the way the setting's other origin-reveals work — a standing hook, not handed to the player at creation. A GM can let a Sown character go an entire campaign never learning this. If it does come up, it should land the way Testament-tier reveals do elsewhere in this project (Vigil dossier, capstone): rare, and heavy when it finally happens.

You didn't grow up believing. You woke up already believing, fully formed, with nothing behind it — no childhood catechism, no crisis of doubt, no moment you can point to and call your conversion. Just faith, present and complete, the way a heartbeat is present and complete, attached to a body that remembers nothing before the day it started. You've built an entire life around the assumption that this makes you chosen. Marked out specifically, deliberately, for something. Nobody's told you otherwise. Nobody's told you anything at all.

cinderfall.foundAmong: Found among: pairs with the Reckoner's Singularity Source (Reckoner dossier, §2/§8) — no named deity, no congregation, and no two of them who've ever met
